clue.text: Go against the grain of American breakfasts?

definitions.text: Go against the grain of American breakfasts?

parts.note: to buck is to resist or go against something, as in bucking a trend
wheat is the grain most often meant by the word

explanation.surface: Someone rebels against the cereal Americans eat in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: pancakes made from this grain are an American breakfast staple. 'Go against the grain' reads as an idiom, but splits into BUCK and WHEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Its seeds are ground into flour for the griddle cakes served at American breakfasts.

clue.text: Money means entanglement in evil

indicators.note: in places the tangle inside the word for evil, which is split around it

parts.note: a bane is a curse or source of harm
a knot is a tangle of string or hair

explanation.surface: Money is said to cause tangles of wrongdoing, as in the root of all evil.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper note issued by a bank is a form of money.

clue.text: Playing hard to get backup from American invader

parts.note: someone coy feigns reluctance, playing hard to get

indicators.note: the word backup splits as back and up, so up is turned back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flirtatious foreigner retreats from someone who has invaded from America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backup' looks like one word for support, but it splits: 'back' turns 'up' round to give PU.
explanation.definitionFit: This large South American rodent has spread through Europe and elsewhere as an invasive species.

clue.text: A check on her identity contrived to pass Helen, and she had a chitchat with Faustus

definitions.text: A check on her identity contrived to pass Helen, and she had a chitchat with Faustus

parts.words: A check on her identity contrived to pass Helen, and she had a chitchat with Faustus
parts.note: Faustus, in Marlowe's play, meets the conjured Helen of Troy and asks whether she is really the beauty who started the Trojan war: a question checking her identity

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the famous line from Marlowe's Doctor Faustus, spoken when Faustus sees Helen of Troy, whose beauty sent the Greek fleet to Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation is Faustus's wondering question to Helen, which checks that she is the legendary beauty.

clue.text: Spike at French city during the first part

parts.note: an ear is the spike of grain on a cereal plant
Lyon is a major city in France

explanation.surface: A sharp rise hits a city in France during the opening phase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening near the beginning of a period happens at an initial stage, before much time has passed.

clue.text: Cat makes water

definitions.meaning: a stock pet name for a cat in Britain, like Rover for a dog
a childish British word for urinating, to tiddle, in its third person form

explanation.surface: A pet cat relieves itself.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a traditional British pet cat's name and a nursery word for passing urine.

clue.text: See 3
Shrew's connection shown in anguish or tension

indicators.note: shown in says the letters are on display within the words anguish or tension

explanation.surface: A nagging spouse's relative displays distress or strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrew' suggests a nagging wife, but means Shakespeare's play The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: He is a character in The Taming of the Shrew, a suitor connected with its plot.

clue.text: Quality of wood warped at end

indicators.note: warped at end says only the closing pair of letters of the word for wood is twisted round

parts.note: timber is wood used for building

explanation.surface: A plank of good grade has gone bent at one end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warped at end' turns only the last two letters: ER becomes RE.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tonal quality or colour of a sound, distinct from pitch and loudness.

clue.text: Cortes and Co. that squint producer loves

definitions.text: Cortes and Co. that squint producer loves

parts.note: Co. is the standard abbreviation for company

indicators.note: a producer makes something new, so the letters of squint are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: adores means loves

explanation.surface: Cortes and his companions are adored by the man who makes people squint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'producer' is the anagram signal, making something new from 'squint'. Cortes led the Spanish conquest of Mexico, and the whole clue describes him and his men.
explanation.definitionFit: Cortes and his fellow Spanish conquerors of the Americas are known collectively by this name.

clue.text: Can't Alfred make up his mind?

definitions.text: Can't Alfred make up his mind?

parts.words: Can't Alfred make up his mind?
parts.note: an indecisive person keeps saying no and then saying yes; this pair of words is also the surname of the poet Alfred who wrote The Highwayman

explanation.walkthrough: Alfred is the English poet Alfred Noyes; split, his surname is a refusal followed by agreement, the sound of someone who can't decide.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the poet Alfred, author of The Highwayman, reads as a dithering reply.

clue.text: Means of reproduction to do with marriage? Pointless, weird

indicators.note: weird marks the letters as strangely arranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: pointless takes away a compass point, here the letter for east

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something about how marriage produces offspring seems odd and futile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means of reproduction' suggests breeding, but means playing back sound. 'Pointless' drops E (east) from MARRIAGE, leaving MARRIAG; 'weird' scrambles that with DO.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiogram was a radio and record player in one cabinet, used to play back recorded music.

clue.text: Bad part of summer at its height in American city

indicators.note: in places the month and height inside the city's letters

parts.note: NY is short for New York
Aug is short for August, a summer month

explanation.surface: Something bad happens in a US city when summer is at its peak.
explanation.definitionFit: Naughty describes misbehaving, as a bad child does.

clue.text: Benedictine question with place about right?

indicators.note: about means the word for place goes round the question abbreviation

parts.note: lieu is place, as in in lieu of

explanation.surface: A Benedictine monk asks about a location being correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Benedictine' looks like a monk, but is the brandy-based liqueur of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedictine is a herbal liqueur, an example of the drink type.

clue.text: See 3
Clear behind? Go higher still at bridge

parts.note: overt means open, plain to see
rump is the backside or behind

explanation.surface: Someone climbs clear of the rear and gets higher on a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: In the card game bridge, to overtrump is to play a higher trump than one already played.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, playing a trump higher than an earlier trump on the same trick is the term.

clue.text: Frith's colour returns while it's light

definitions.note: a possessive standing for the painting by Frith, a noun

indicators.note: returns signals that the colour word comes back reversed

parts.note: red is a colour
by means during, as in by night
day is the time when it is light

explanation.surface: A man named Frith's tint comes back during daylight hours.
explanation.walkthrough: William Powell Frith painted The Derby Day, a crowded scene at the Epsom horse race; 'returns' turns RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian painter Frith's best-known work is the crowded racecourse panorama of this title.

clue.text: Tire out, then handle gently — last of the cycle

parts.note: to exhaust is to wear out completely
to stroke is to touch softly

explanation.surface: Wear someone out, then soothe them, at the end of a bike ride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycle' suggests a bicycle, but is the four-stroke engine cycle.
explanation.definitionFit: In a four-stroke engine, the final phase expels burnt gases from the cylinder.

clue.text: Leg it with us, moving furthest from fair

indicators.note: moving says the letters shift into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Run away with us, heading as far as we can from the fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' looks like a funfair, but means beautiful.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair means good-looking, so the least attractive is the furthest from it.

clue.text: The highest level one's required to talk on

parts.note: taken as written
to prate is to talk on and on foolishly

explanation.surface: A tax band is the most anyone must pay, and the right to speak on.
explanation.walkthrough: The highest level is the top tax band, the one people are required to pay at.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest band of income tax, paid on the top slice of earnings.

clue.text: Godhead after a 25

parts.note: poll is an old word for the head, as in a poll tax
the solution to 25 across means circular, and a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A deity comes after a round of the canon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Godhead' looks like one word, but splits: 'God' is the definition and 'head' gives POLL.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo was the Greek and Roman god of music, poetry and the sun.

clue.text: Mine (if I hear you have left) is pathetic

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine
taken as written

indicators.note: hear says the word is to be taken as heard, a letter sounding like it

parts.note: the letter U is said just like you

explanation.surface: A coal mine is a pitiful place if you've left it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitiful describes something that arouses pity, which is what pathetic means.

clue.text: Backing bread roll without drink not right: there's no fuel in it

indicators.note: backing means the whole assembly is read from the end to the start
without means outside, so the roll wraps around the drink

parts.note: a bap is a soft bread roll in Britain

indicators.note: not removes the letter for right from the drink

parts.note: cider is an alcoholic apple drink

explanation.surface: A bread roll eaten without a drink isn't right: there's nothing in it to keep you going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking. 'not right' removes the R from the drink, leaving CIDE, and 'Backing' turns the whole assembled roll round.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedicab is a pedal-powered rickshaw, so it runs on muscle rather than fuel.

clue.text: Fool, friend to prince

parts.note: a chum is a friend

explanation.surface: A jester is pal to a prince.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump is a foolish person, a dupe.

clue.text: See 3
The canon should be shot

definitions.meaning: a musical canon, in which voices enter in turn singing the same tune
a single bullet or shell, one discharge of a gun, is meant to be fired

explanation.surface: The clergyman ought to be executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' suggests a churchman, or a cannon, but is the musical form; the second sense is a cartridge for firing.
explanation.definitionFit: It means both a song sung in staggered canon, like Frère Jacques, and a unit of ammunition.

clue.text: I shouldn't have said that nothing works

parts.note: O is the figure zero, nothing
ops is short for opera, the plural of opus, a work

explanation.surface: An apology for a careless remark: nothing is working.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is what someone says after a blunder or a slip of the tongue.

clue.text: Blavatsky's boy and girl?

definitions.note: a possessive standing for the doctrine of Madame Blavatsky, a noun

parts.note: Theo is a boy's name
Sophy is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Two children belonging to a Russian mystic.
explanation.walkthrough: Helena Blavatsky founded the Theosophical Society in 1875.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Blavatsky founded the mystical doctrine of this name, so it is her movement.
